title: Sunset Valley refrigerator alarm runbook
brief: Sunset Valley Food Share needs a short runbook for volunteers when the walk-in refrigerator alarm sounds or the display reads above 41 degrees Fahrenheit, to be read on phones in the warehouse; owned by the Operations Manager, effective 2026-11-01. Section "First two minutes": silence the alarm, check the door is fully closed, read the display and the backup thermometer inside, and write the time on the log sheet. Section "Decide what to do": if the temperature is 41 to 45 degrees and has been above 41 for less than 2 hours, move dairy, eggs, meat and prepared meals into the backup chest freezers right away, keep produce in place, and call the refrigeration technician; if it is above 45 degrees, or has been above 41 for 2 hours or more, or nobody knows how long, the dairy, eggs, meat and prepared meals must be thrown away with a second volunteer present to confirm; produce, canned and packaged goods can stay. Section "Steps in order": 1 call ChillRight, the refrigeration vendor, on 555-0134 (open 24 hours) and ask for a 4-hour response; 2 message the Operations Manager; 3 move or discard items as above; 4 record each item thrown away on the waste log with its weight in pounds; 5 after the repair, run the refrigerator for 4 hours below 38 degrees before restocking. Make sure nobody ever tastes or sniffs food to decide whether it is safe. Finish with "Contacts": Operations Manager, Delphine Okonkwo; ChillRight on-call line, 555-0134; Food safety lead, Bram Verhoeven.

edit.request: Change the warning threshold from 41 to 40 degrees and the restock rule to 6 hours below 38 degrees, and add a contact: Facilities volunteer, Anika Rao.
